Notes

A loop of distrust opens into underworld property sales and a borrowed lighter. The final cube makes the problem visual: a person has more faces than you can see at once.

白眼狼

白眼狼 names someone who repays kindness with ingratitude or betrayal. The wolf is not merely dangerous; its offense is relational, because care has already been given. Pairing that insult with “can’t be trusted” for much of the opening makes the verdict arrive before the story. The later disclosure of his whereabouts supplies the breach behind that relentless judgment.

  • Genius community transcript
柴米油盐不进

柴米油盐 names the basic household staples—firewood, rice, oil and salt. The line folds that phrase into 油盐不进, refusing all persuasion, literally letting neither oil nor salt in. The expanded version makes the other person resistant to the whole material language of ordinary life: nothing practical, familiar or necessary seems able to get through.

  • Genius community transcript
小伙伴

小伙伴 is a friendly, slightly childlike term for companions. Setting it beside “gave away my whereabouts” makes the intimacy accusatory. These were people close enough to know where he was, which is precisely why their betrayal mattered. The cute name survives after trust is gone, making it more bitter than a straightforward enemy label.

  • Lyric transcript
索命

索 is to demand or exact something; 命 is life. The verb makes vengeance sound like collection, linking the threat to the monetary and personal accounting of “Debt.” Yet within a few lines the speaker says he need not act at all. The verse moves between personally enforcing the balance and imagining that a larger order will settle it.

  • Lyric transcript
掏心

掏心 is literally taking out the heart, but figuratively opening oneself with complete sincerity. The warning follows a threat to claim lives and is followed by the claim that nobody can be trusted. That placement makes emotional openness feel like bodily exposure.

  • Lyric text
爱命且惜命

爱 and 惜 are close but not identical: loving life and taking care not to lose it. Between revenge threats and proverbial advice, the phrase briefly sounds like guidance for staying alive. The repeated 命 links self-preservation to the enemy’s life demanded earlier, making survival and menace parts of the same vocabulary.

  • Lyric transcript
失败是成功的母亲

This is a version of the familiar maxim 失败是成功之母: failure can lead to success. In its surroundings, however, the lesson learned is distrust, and the next proverb promises that bad people will be punished by other bad people. A consoling saying is recruited into a sequence about surviving betrayal.

  • Lyric text
恶人自有恶人磨

恶人自有恶人磨 promises that one bad person will eventually meet another capable of tormenting them. The repetition of 恶人 leaves justice morally impure: the punisher need not be good. The following appeal to heaven offers a second version of the same relief, allowing the speaker to imagine a reckoning without doing the work himself.

  • Genius community transcript
新楼盘开售

新楼盘开售 is the language of a new property development opening for sale. 地府 relocates that sales pitch to the realm of the dead. Instead of merely wishing an enemy dead, the line treats their afterlife accommodation as a product ready to move.

  • Lyric text
纸钱

纸钱 here is ritual paper money burned for spirits or the dead, rather than ordinary banknotes. It follows the underworld property sale and precedes the borrowed lighter and fire. Knowing that use ties the apparently separate images of purchasing, death, paper, and burning together.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 紙錢
  • Lyric text
火机借我

This begins as a tiny ordinary request. The next line anticipates the ordinary explanation—smoking—only to replace it with arson. Coming straight after ritual paper money, the lighter is the hinge between a recognizable act of burning offerings and a wildly enlarged fire. Its mundane scale makes the jump more absurd.

  • Lyric transcript
从春天烧到冬天

The fire is assigned the length of an entire year. Instead of a momentary flare of anger, it becomes something that persists across seasons, answered soon afterward by “so many years” of still not understanding people. The extravagant duration gives distrust its own weather: this is anger imagined as a condition one lives through.

  • Lyric transcript
新鲜

新鲜 can mean fresh, novel or surprising. The profane rhetorical remark sounds unimpressed, undercutting the spectacular revenge scene it has just produced. Before the cube arrives, the verse briefly treats the cycle of betrayal and threatened punishment as something tiresomely familiar, even when its imagery is fantastically excessive.

  • Lyric transcript
好多面

面 is a side or surface and also an aspect of a person. The final 魔方, Rubik’s cube, turns the familiar idea of a many-sided person into a manipulable puzzle. Years of acquaintance have not solved it. The cube also limits any single view: seeing one face clearly does not tell you what is happening on the others.

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
